analysis.title: Meta Platforms Inc. (META): Equity Offering Announced; Recent Earnings Highlighted Early Muse Success, Core Business Momentum & Intent to Remain Focused on Scaling Investments
key_insights: Meta announced on October 26 an equity-financing plan of about $95bn in two parts: about $35bn of immediate underwritten offerings and an additional about $60bn at-the-market (ATM) equity program.

The $35bn immediate raise is about $22.5bn of Class A common stock, structured with forward-sale agreements, plus about 250mm Series A depositary shares in a mandatory convertible preferred, totaling about $12.5bn.
Nvidia, AMD and Broadcom (all covered by Jim Schneider) have indicated interest in buying up to an aggregate of about $5bn of Class A shares in the common stock offering, severally and not jointly.

The about $60bn ATM program is expected to begin after trading starts in Meta's previously announced Class C common stock. The company said it is not expected to commence until Q1 2027 and that definitive agreements, timing, size and terms are not finalized.

Q3'26 earnings showed a clear beat and optimism on core business operating momentum, early successes for Muse, a framing of further AI-related revenue paths (SMB, enterprise), and a reiteration of plans to scale AI infrastructure investment.

Meta announced a plan to issue non-voting Class C shares so the founder/CEO can retain voting control in scenarios such as multi-year investments and a California wealth tax. GS views the scenarios in the filing as a range of possibilities the Board analyzed, not financial forecasts.
Investor debates after earnings centered on (a) timing, magnitude and form of potential capital raises and (b) clarity on 2027 and later AI investment plans.
GS projects FY27/28 total GAAP expenses of about $221bn / $254bn and total capex of about $230bn / $250bn, for cumulative GAAP expenses of about $475bn and capex of about $480bn across the two years.

GS reiterates Buy and a 12-month price target of $885, with no changes to forward estimates. At $634 the stock trades at about 20x / 17x GS 2027/28 GAAP EPS (ex-cash), with no adjustment for funds raised in the offerings.

GS estimates free cash flow falls from $46.1bn in 2025 to $6.4bn in 2026E and -$33.5bn in 2027E, with capex of $136.7bn in 2026E and $223.4bn in 2027E, and net debt rising as long-term debt grows to about $100.9bn in 2026E.
Goldman Sachs is acting as manager or co-manager of the pending underwriting of the Meta offering, which is a disclosed conflict of interest.

market_movers.rationale: GS keeps its core thesis on AI and spatial computing across Family of Apps and Reality Labs and makes no estimate changes after the offering announcement. Price target implies 37.7% upside from $642.62.

sector_views.rationale: GS sees Meta as well-positioned against several long-term secular growth themes across its coverage universe and rates it Buy.

earnings_insights: Meta Q3'26 earnings (reported, before the 10/26 note): clear beat and optimism on core business momentum per GS, with early Muse successes disclosed. The note gives no EPS or revenue figures for the print.

GS EPS (diluted, pre-exceptionals) estimates: $23.49 for FY2025, $28.84 for FY2026E, $31.02 for FY2027E, $37.49 for FY2028E. Quarterly estimates are $3.83 for 9/26, $8.39 for 12/26E, $7.16 for 3/27E and $6.77 for 6/27E.
GS revenue estimates: $200,965mn for FY2025, $257,185mn for FY2026E, $315,886mn for FY2027E, $374,132mn for FY2028E, with growth of 28.0% in 2026E, 22.8% in 2027E and 18.4% in 2028E.
GS EBIT margin estimates: 41.4% in 2025, 31.2% in 2026E, 29.9% in 2027E, 32.2% in 2028E. Gross margin falls from 82.0% to 78.7%, 68.3% and 68.1% over the same years.
risk_factors: Competition for user growth, engagement and advertising dollars from incumbent and emerging internet, media and commerce companies.
Large investments in long-tailed initiatives could depress operating margins for longer than GS forecasts.
No or low levels of incremental shareholder returns going forward.
Regulatory scrutiny and industry practices could alter the business model.
Antitrust scrutiny could hinder M&A (talent and product) or lead to a break-up or dis-synergies of prior M&A.
Inability to monetize upside opportunities in messaging, social commerce, AI (including Muse) and Reality Labs.
Exposure to global macro volatility and investor risk appetite for growth stocks.
vol_and_positioning: Meta's equity raise includes about $60bn of ATM issuance planned for 2027 onward, a potential supply overhang. GS makes no valuation adjustment for it.
Share performance: META is +6.0% over 3 months, -2.5% over 6 months and -12.4% over 12 months, versus the S&P 500 by +3.0%, -9.1% and -22.6% relative.
